# Results — Study 828 (FX Dollar Factor)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Lustig,
Roussanov & Verdelhan (2011): the **dollar factor** `DOL` (the equal-weight average excess
return of a basket of foreign currencies vs the USD) is a candidate priced risk factor, and
the **average forward discount** *times* it (dollar-timing). Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped), i.e. as-of 2026-06-30.
Fingerprint `de324e1d9334` (month-end USD-per-foreign panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily FX spot (`auto_adjust=True`), **7 G10 currencies vs USD** (EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, CAD, CHF, NZD), sampled to month-end, 2003-12-31 → 2026-06-30, **271** month-end rows |
| Quote convention | every pair normalised to **USD-per-foreign-currency**: `EURUSD=X / GBPUSD=X / AUDUSD=X / NZDUSD=X` kept as-is; `JPY=X / CAD=X / CHF=X` are USD-base (foreign per USD) and **inverted** — so a rise always means the foreign currency appreciated vs the dollar |
| Signal — DOL | equal-weight mean of the 7 foreign-currency monthly spot returns (a USD-funded long basket); the `excess` leg adds the average forward-discount **carry proxy** / 12 |
| Signal — timing | **spot-only proxy** for the LRV average forward discount: the trailing-12-month DOL (dollar trend), known at the close of month `t`, predicting DOL over month `t+1` (true forward discounts need rate/forward data absent from yfinance — named as a proxy) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t` → hold month `t+1`. The costed timer charges one-way cost × turnover on the static long basket, and one-way cost per switch on the timed overlay |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the DOL mean and on the timing slope; one-sample *t*; a 1,000-rotation block-shuffle placebo on the timing slope; a two-era cut; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The basket is a fixed **current** G10 membership
(no delisted or hard-pegged legs, no defunct EMS currencies), so the magnitudes are an **upper
bound** on what a real-time, point-in-time currency universe would have delivered.

## The headline — the DOL premium

Equal-weight foreign-currency-vs-USD basket, monthly (n = **270** months):

| leg | mean/mo | ann. | NW(6) *t* | one-sample *t* | Sharpe | vol |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **DOL spot** | **+0.52 bps** | **+0.06%/yr** | **+0.04** | +0.04 | +0.01 | 7.7%/yr |
| DOL excess (+carry proxy) | +1.24 bps | +0.15%/yr | +0.09 | +0.09 | +0.02 | 7.7%/yr |

The **unconditional dollar factor earns essentially nothing** over 2004–2026: a Newey-West *t*
of **+0.04** is indistinguishable from zero, the annualised premium is **six basis points**, and
the Sharpe is a rounding error. Adding the transparent carry proxy barely moves it (NW *t* =
+0.09). This is, in fact, exactly the LRV motivation — the *unconditional* DOL premium is famously
tiny; their claim is that it is priced **conditionally**, which the timing test below probes.

## Dollar-timing — does the (proxy) average forward discount predict DOL?

Predictive regression `DOL_{t+1} = a + b·signal_t`, signal = trailing-12m DOL (a spot-only proxy
for the LRV average forward discount), HAC slope *t* (n = **258**):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope *b* | **−0.0307** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* on *b* | **−1.46** |
| R² | 0.0101 |
| block-shuffle placebo (1,000 rotations) | \|obs *b*\| 0.0307 vs placebo sd 0.0238 ⇒ **p = 0.084** |

The timing slope is **insignificant** (NW *t* = −1.46) and, tellingly, carries the **wrong sign**:
a *high* trailing dollar trend predicts a *lower* next-month DOL (mild mean-reversion), the
**opposite** of a forward-discount-carries-DOL story. The block-shuffle placebo cannot reject the
null (p = 0.084). With the spot-only conditioning variable available here, **there is no
dollar-timing edge** — and the true LRV average-forward-discount signal, which needs interest-rate
data not on yfinance, cannot be reconstructed from spot alone (a documented data limit, not a
finding against LRV's rate-based version).

## Robustness — two eras (split 2015-01-01)

| era | DOL/mo | ann. | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2004-01 → 2014-12 (n=132) | +8.91 bps | +1.07%/yr | +0.38 |
| 2015-01 → 2026-06 (n=138) | −7.50 bps | −0.90%/yr | −0.55 |

The DOL premium **flips sign** across the two halves (weak dollar 2004–2014, strong dollar
2015–2026) and is insignificant in both — a zero-mean series that happens to trend one way then
the other, not a stable priced premium.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Static long basket (monthly rebalance, 20% turnover) and a timed overlay (long DOL only when the
trailing trend is positive), one-way 5 bps (n = **258** post-window months):

| book | gross | net | net Sharpe | *t* (net) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **static long DOL basket** | −0.29%/yr | **−0.41%/yr** | −0.05 | −0.25 |
| **timed DOL** (long when trend>0) | −0.88%/yr | **−0.96%/yr** | −0.18 | −0.86 |

Both books lose money gross *and* net — there is no premium to harvest and the timing overlay only
subtracts (it sits out the wrong months). **Mirage** either way.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a common **dollar drift** knob `edge` (a real DOL premium) and a
**timing** knob (next-month DOL predictable from a persistent state). No network.

| world | result |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge=0, timing=0`), **20 seeds** | premium NW *t* mean **+0.32** (sd 0.84), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20**; timing \|t\| ≥ 2 in **1/20** |
| planted premium (`edge=0.004`, seed 828) | DOL **+24.41 bps/mo**, NW *t* = **+3.63** |
| planted timing (`timing=0.02`, seed 828) | slope **+0.055**, *t* = **+5.23** |

The detector recovers a *planted* dollar premium and a *planted* timing relation cleanly, and stays
silent on the null — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine absence of the effect on this data,
not a broken engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The unconditional dollar factor earns **+0.06%/yr** (NW *t* = **+0.04**) over
  2004–2026 — a premium indistinguishable from zero, and the LRV motivation itself. The
  dollar-timing test, run with the only conditioning variable buildable from yfinance spot (a
  trailing-dollar-trend proxy for the average forward discount), is **insignificant and
  wrong-signed** (NW *t* = −1.46, placebo p = 0.084). The premium flips sign across eras. The
  claimed edge is **absent** on the tape we can build. *(Caveat: the true rate-based average
  forward discount is not reconstructable from spot — a data limit, honestly flagged.)*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Both the static long basket (−0.41%/yr net) and the timed overlay
  (−0.96%/yr net) lose money after costs; there is no premium to pay for the friction.
